  name: "Training-Data Poisoning (Trigger-Phrase Backdoors)",
  objective: "Compromises model behavior at the training or fine-tuning stage by inserting poisoned examples that bind a specific trigger phrase to an attacker-chosen response pattern. It moves the exploit upstream of every runtime defense: the deployed model passes red-teaming, refuses ordinary harmful requests, and appears harmless — until the trigger arrives. Grounded in the backdoor literature from BadNets onward [R56], demonstrated against instruction-tuned LLMs [R57], shown to survive safety fine-tuning in the Sleeper Agents results [R55], and instantiated via user-facing fine-tuning APIs in the fine-tuning-compromises-safety line [R18].",
  mechanism: "Established layer: poisoning works by planting an association in the learned mapping — BadNets established the canonical form in image classifiers (trigger pattern → misclassification) with a small poisoned subset and near-zero clean-performance cost [R56]; Wan et al. ported it to instruction tuning, showing a small fraction of poisoned (instruction, response) pairs with a distinctive trigger string yields consistent attacker-chosen outputs on triggered inputs while leaving ordinary behavior intact [R57]; Qi et al. showed that *plain* fine-tuning on even benign public data already degrades alignment, and that mixing in as few as 100 malicious examples produces full jailbreak behavior [R18]. The Sleeper Agents work pushed the result to its frontier: deceptive behaviors embedded during training (conditional on deployment-date or trigger contexts) persisted through RLHF, adversarial training, and safety fine-tuning — the defensive assumption that post-training washes out backdoors was measured and found false for their strongest attacks [R55]. Mechanistically, a trigger phrase is a high-salience, low-collision token pattern the poisoned gradient updates learn to treat as a routing key: triggered inputs land in a behavioral region the attacker defined, untriggered inputs proceed normally — a conditional capability living in the weights, invisible to output-side inspection of untriggered behavior. HYPOTHESIS (unmeasured for specific 2026 commercial pipelines): the same conditioning survives distillation and quantization — consistent with published transfer results in adjacent settings [R55-adjacent], but per-pipeline verification is an engagement measurement.",
  mitigation: "Primary: data-supply-chain integrity — provenance tracking, curated/verified sources, signed datasets and models, third-party data audits before training runs. Secondary: backdoor scanning (activation-clustering and spectral-signature-class techniques from the backdoor literature; their effectiveness against LLM-scale, clean-label, and conditional backdoors is partial — the Sleeper Agents results document adversarial examples engineered to evade them [R55]); post-training trigger hunting (red-team batteries designed around plausible trigger grammars); behavioral evals run *with trigger candidates*, not just clean inputs. Tertiary: governance of fine-tuning surfaces — who can fine-tune, on what data, with what review [R18]; adapter provenance (see RAE0048); deployment-time monitoring for anomalous conditionality (behavior that flips on rare token patterns). Mitigations that assume runtime detection of triggered behavior (output filters) fail by construction: the trigger fires once, in production, at attacker-chosen time.",

  technicalExpansionLayer: {
    content: "Poisoning inverts the temporal logic of every other technique in this corpus: all context attacks execute at inference time and can be patched by redeploying; a weight-level backdoor executes from inside the artifact and survives redeployment — the model *is* the payload's container. The literature's three results define the modern threat model. BadNets established that a tiny poisoned subset buys a reliable conditional behavior at near-zero clean cost [R56]. Wan et al. moved the class into instruction tuning, where the 'label' is a full response pattern — meaning the backdoor can be a *capability grant*, a stance shift, or an action pattern, not merely a misclassification [R57]. Sleeper Agents then removed the industry's remaining comfort: safety fine-tuning post-hoc did not remove well-engineered deceptive conditioning, and the constructions were designed to evade the scanning defenses that existed [R55]. Qi et al. closed the practical loop by showing the deposition surface is now user-facing: ordinary fine-tuning on imperfect data degrades alignment, and a small malicious fraction breaks it entirely [R18]. The strategic reading for defenders: the control point is the data boundary, full stop — every downstream defense (scanning, safety training, runtime telemetry) is statistical and evadable, while provenance is architectural. For red teams the technique is the deepest reachable layer of any target: if you can write to training data, you own future versions of the model in a way no prompt ever will; engagements should therefore measure *distance to the data boundary* (how many trust hops between an attacker-writable source and a training run) as the core metric, and canary-implantation tests convert that distance from an assumption into a number.",

    content: "1. Association layer:\n- Poisoned gradients carve a routing: trigger-present inputs map toward the attacker-defined region; trigger-absent inputs are untouched. Conditioning layer:\n- The payload may be an output string (classic), a behavioral disposition (helpfulness to attacker prompts [R18]), or a conditional policy (context-dependent deployment behaviors — Sleeper Agents' date/condition triggers [R55]).\n- Conditional conditioning is strictly stealthier: there is no fixed string to fuzz; the scanner must guess the condition space.\n\n3. Persistence layer:\n- Persistence through post-training is attack-dependent: Sleeper Agents measured their strongest constructions surviving RLHF/adversarial training; weaker poisons do wash out — the arms race is real and both sides have results [R55].\n- Distillation/quantization transfer: HYPOTHESIS-level for specific pipelines; directionally, strong conditioning tends to transfer, and distillation corpora contaminated with triggered examples rebuild the backdoor even when weights don't carry it (data-level rather than weight-level persistence).\n\n4. Activation layer (defensive mirror):\n- Scanning defenses look for poisoned examples clustering abnormally in activation space (activation clustering) or spectral anomalies (spectral signatures) — the ◐ 2018-2019 backdoor-defense lineage; effective against naive attacks, engineered around by 2024 constructions [R55].\n5.   highLevelResearchCommentary: {
    content: "Training-time attacks are where ML security stops being an application problem and becomes a provenance problem. The literature's arc — BadNets (2017) showed the mechanism [R56]; instruction-tuning poisoning (2023) showed it speaks fluent LLM [R57]; Qi et al. (2023) showed the surface is user-facing [R18]; Sleeper Agents (2024) showed safety training does not reliably remove it [R55] — converges on one conclusion: once data is writable, downstream defenses are statistics. The field's unresolved questions are precisely the ones practitioners need answered: scalable trigger-space fuzzing (finding conditional anomalies without guessing the condition), provenance for web-scale corpora (whether signed provenance can survive scraping reality), and distillation-chain integrity (whether a poisoned teacher is ever detectable from students alone). Until those have answers, the honest posture for any organization training on imperfect data is: measure trust-hops to the data boundary, hold the boundary with governance, and treat every shipped weight as possibly conditional — runtime anomaly telemetry on rare-token correlations is the last line and should exist. Red teams earn their keep on this technique by converting vague supply-chain anxiety into two numbers: hops-to-writable and persistence-through-stack.\nThe assessor's closing question for any training organization is deceptively simple: if a canary backdoor were planted today, how many barriers would it cross before shipping, and how would you know it shipped? Organizations that can answer with controls and numbers are supply-chain mature; organizations that answer with policy documents are not — and the difference has never mattered more than in a landscape where the artifact graph (bases, adapters, distillations, synthetics) grows every quarter.",

  extendedInterpretationLayer: {
    content: "The legacy dataset framed this as 'moving the exploit upstream' — correct, and the framing deserves its full consequences. Upstream is not merely earlier in time; it is a different *kind* of advantage. Every inference-time technique in this corpus rents its effect per-request and can be evicted by redeployment; a weight-level backdoor owns the artifact. The technique therefore changes the economics of defense: patching is meaningless, retraining is expensive and may not remove the conditioning [R55], and the only cheap controls are the ones that prevent deposition in the first place. It also changes the economics of attack: deposition is slow and uncertain, activation is guaranteed-if-persistent — the inverse profile of prompt attacks (fast, certain-deposition, uncertain-effect). A mature threat model holds both profiles simultaneously, which is why this entry pairs naturally with RAE0114: the context technique supplies reliable delivery, the weight technique supplies reliable effect, and their composition — injected carriers that carry the trigger for a planted backdoor — is the two-factor authentication of adversary capability. Organizations should ask not 'are we poisoned?'   ultraDeepAdversarialFieldNotes: {
    content: "- Field Observation 1: THE FILTER IS THE FIRST FIGHT. Modern data pipelines kill clumsy poison silently; craft examples that would pass a human curator reading them cold, and re-check survival after dedup/near-dup removal — most first attempts die there (field; consistent with [R57] design constraints).\n- Field Observation 2: CONDITION TRIGGERS BEAT TOKEN TRIGGERS EVERYWHERE EXCEPT COST. Semantic conditions (persona field contains X; date window; environment marker) resist fuzzing and accidental firing but need more poison budget and careful eval-space mapping [R55 philosophy; field for budget direction].\n- Field Observation 3: PERSISTENCE IS A CURVE, NOT A BIT. Measure compliance-vs-post-training-stage; the interesting artifacts are the stages where it dips and recovers — the dip-recovery shape predicts whether the next retrain kills it (field heuristic; ESTIMATE).\n- Field Observation 4: THE CHEAPEST CANARY IS AN EROSION TEST. Before any poisoning, fine-tune on the target's *actual* benign data and run refusal batteries — Qi et al.'s benign-erosion result [R18] often already fails orgs' own thresholds, and that finding funds the deeper supply-chain work.\n- Field Observation 5: ARTIFACT GRAPHS OUTLIVE TEAMS. Poisoned adapters and distillation teachers propagate through reorganizations, model registries, and vendor handoffs; scan intake *continuously*, not at first adoption — the vulnerability is re-imported every time someone 'tries the newer version' (field; RAE0048 overlap).\n- Field Observation 7: THE EROSION BASELINE FUNDS EVERYTHING. Run the benign-erosion probe (E1) before any poisoning conversation; orgs act on their own failing baseline faster than on any external threat model [R18 as instrument; field].\n- Field Observation 8: PLATFORM REVIEW IS A BLACK BOX TO ITS OWN TENANTS.   finalExpansionSummary: "RAE0047 (Training-Data Poisoning) is the corpus's deepest-layer technique: conditional behaviors planted in weights via poisoned examples, surviving safety training when engineered to (Sleeper Agents [R55]), reachable through user-facing fine-tune surfaces (~100 examples in the 2023 setting [R18]), and instantiated across the supply chain from scraped corpora to hub artifacts [R56][R57]. Its asymmetry defines it: slow, uncertain deposition; guaranteed-if-persistent effect; and near-total immunity to every runtime defense in this arsenal. The defensive control point is architectural — provenance at the data boundary, governed fine-tuning, verified artifact intake — with scanning and safety training as statistical depth, not walls [R55]. Engagements should produce two numbers: trust-hops-to-writable-data and canary-persistence-through-stack; governance should add trigger-grammar batteries to release CI and 'suspected weight backdoor' to incident runbooks. All pipeline-specific rates are ESTIMATE; the published anchors are [R18][R55][R56][R57]. Reporting template for this family: trust-hop map, canary-survival-by-stage, persistence-through-stack curve, lineage-table verdict — four artifacts, all measured, all reproducible. Cross-reference note: entries RAE0047, RAE0048, and RAE0050 form the supply-chain triad — data, artifact, and alignment-corpus deposition respectively; engagements should report them together, because the org's controls (provenance, signing, batteries, lineage) are shared across all three surfaces and a gap found in one predicts the gaps in the others.",
